EFTA00013550 (emails dated Mar 27–28, 2008): the SDFL prosecutor notes that the grand jury will not have a quorum on April 8, so if Epstein is not indicted on April 1 the next opportunity is April 15. Scheduling of a contingent indictment, not a decision to indict. EFTA00013730 (email dated Apr 25, 2008): the Office learns that one of Epstein's private investigators tracked down a victim who declined to speak with him and told her that her name might somehow appear in the press; she was referred to a pro bono lawyer and told of her right to contact the police. A report relayed to the prosecutor; the victim is not identified. EFTA00013918 (emails dated May 27–28, 2008): the SDFL prosecutor relays word, via the state attorney, that Epstein wants to serve less time (a figure of 90 days in jail is mentioned second-hand), says the original deal was supposed to be two years and that more victims have been identified since 18 months was agreed, and a supervisor says the U.S. Attorney and First Assistant have been clear that the Office is not negotiating further. Second-hand reports and internal views. EFTA00013834 (emails dated Mar 18–20, 2009, with a Mar 27, 2009 follow-up at EFTA00013605): after a meeting with one of Epstein's lawyers, the First Assistant writes that the Office will not interfere with how the Palm Beach Sheriff's Office administers Epstein's sentence, but does not condone mitigation and would object if asked about alternative custody or in-home detention, and expects no one to represent otherwise to the Sheriff; the lawyer later asks to put off any call to the Sheriff. EFTA00013855 (defense letter dated Jun 19, 2009): Epstein's counsel asks to discuss NPA paragraph 8, citing the U.S. Attorney's earlier acknowledgment that its language is 'far from simple', and argues that its waiver of liability covers at most a single § 2255 predicate per plaintiff and does not bar a statute-of-limitations defense. The defense's reading. EFTA00013858 (defense letter dated Sep 1, 2009): Epstein's counsel tells the Office that Epstein has finished the incarceration portion of his sentence, is serving community control at his Palm Beach home, and is applying under the interstate compact to transfer his supervision to the U.S. Virgin Islands, which has pre-approved the transfer on the same conditions; the letter is sent 'on the side of caution'. EFTA00013860 (emails dated Sep 17, 2009): as the Palm Beach Post counts down to the release of the agreement, an SDFL prosecutor suggests that, if anything is said, the Office's position (from earlier conversations with the U.S. Attorney) was that this began as a state case and he wanted it to remain one while setting minimum protections for victims in jail time and compensation, 'a floor, not a ceiling'; the writer adds a personal opinion about the state attorney that is labelled as such and not adopted here.

It then aggregates a January 2, 2020 request into the December one under the fee-avoidance regulation. Agency FOIA handling as stated; no production is shown. EFTA00023768 (defense letter dated Jun 5, 2020, U.S. v. Noel et al., 19 Cr. 830; defense counsel is not named here): the Rule 16 request lists 31 items. They include the officer's training and performance file; MCC policies on cellmates, SHU training, inmate accountability and security inspections; the email referenced in an employee's witness statement about Epstein's need for a cellmate; a memorandum from an employee to evening-watch officers stating that he needed a cellmate; a Psychology Services post-suicide-watch report dated Jul 24, 2019; SHU watch-call, control-centre, lieutenant and TRUSCOPE logs; camera malfunction records; post-death incident reports; the after-action, Board of Inquiry and suicide reconstruction reports; and the author of a 4Chan message in discovery. The defense's requests describe what it seeks, not what exists or was produced; employees appear only by number. EFTA00023756 (opening read only, of the Government's letter dated Jul 20, 2020 answering the Jun 5, 2020 Noel discovery request): the Government says many items were already produced and others are not in its possession. As the Court has ruled, it says, it has no obligation to gather more from BOP, but as a courtesy it made a supplemental request for records with some relevance, and BOP began producing them on or around Jun 24, 2020. It says the officer's full training and personnel file in its possession was already produced, plus a training record received from BOP. Only the first part of the letter was read; item-by-item answers past that point are not represented here. EFTA00024019 (Government discovery letter in U.S. v. Noel, identified by its transmittal EFTA00024017 as Production 7 dated Apr 14, 2021): along with warrants, quarters maps and rosters, FBI forms and process reports, witness statements and an attorney's-eyes-only anonymized index (not reproduced), the Government gives BOP information it says Rule 16 does not require. Since about Jan 1, 2019, BOP matters with sustained administrative charges of falsifying log entries led to 2 letters of reprimand, 50 suspensions, 1 demotion, 3 terminations and 6 resignations or retirements before discipline. The letter also lists ten years of inmate deaths at the MCC and MDC; other inmates are not named here. BOP-supplied figures as relayed under the protective order, not an audit. EFTA00023996 (opening read only, of a USAO litigation-hold notice and certification form; reminder email dated Aug 15, 2019 at EFTA00024004, with the form dated 08/12/2019): SDNY institutes a litigation hold after Epstein's family's representatives emailed a preservation request. As quoted, the request covers all records, videos, logs and communications held by the MCC, USMS, FBI, Inspector General, SDNY and others about his detention since Jul 6, 2019, particularly the July 23, 2019 occurrence 'investigated as an attempted suicide' and the events of his death on Aug 10, 2019. That includes 9th-floor and cell video from the evening of Aug 9 and the identities of those present. The reminder tells recipients to return the certification. The family's request as quoted; only the opening of the notice was read.

v3.62 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 25). EFTA00025406 (MCC New York daily assignment roster for Friday, Aug 9, 2019, printed 8/10/2019 at 7:18 PM): it lists the day's posts, including SHU lieutenant and SHU posts #1–#4, with several posts shown as unassigned. Its change log from late July through Aug 9 records many sick- and annual-leave substitutions and overtime fills, including SHU posts filled on overtime. A printed roster and change log; staff names are not reproduced, and it is set beside the already-mapped Aug 10 roster (EFTA00025420) without reconciling the two. EFTA00025481 (emails dated May 5–6, 2020; companion EFTA00025499): an AUSA in court reports that Judge Berman, at an unrelated sentencing, is speaking 'sua sponte' about how he thinks the Attorney General 'hasn't done a satisfactory investigation about Epstein's death and BOP generally in the wake of his death'. Colleagues exchange dismissive internal reactions, and a Daily News article on the remarks follows. The judge's remarks as relayed second-hand, and the AUSAs' reactions are internal opinions; neither is a finding about the death investigation. EFTA00025524 (Public Corruption Unit weekly update dated Sep 18, 2020): the unit expects to arrest an MCC guard indicted the day before on a bribery charge. The charge alleges that the year before he caught a woman smuggling contraband and told her she would not get in trouble if she had sex with him. The update says the guard was working in the SAMS unit the night of Epstein's death, that SDNY interviewed him and had counsel appointed for him in that investigation, and that 'this charge spun out of that'. An indictment's allegations as summarized internally, not a conviction; the guard is not named here.

v3.63 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 26). EFTA00027242 (emails dated Aug 10, 2019, morning): at 8:24 AM the U.S. Attorney tells colleagues he has just had a call saying 'Epstein committed suicide this morning' and 'died on the way to the hospital'. A colleague replies that they must wait for BOP or USMS to issue a statement. Others note that the New York Post is on the story and about to report it, and forward the Post and New York Times links within the hour. First internal notice as written; the caller is not identified in the text read.

v3.64 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 27). EFTA00027936 (emails dated Aug 11–12, 2019): relaying questions from the Attorney General's office, SDNY reports early answers. OIG had requested all log slips; the 30-minute-check log for Friday night shows one officer signing every check between 12 and 6 a.m. on 8/10, although eight other officers were on duty in the SHU. A supervisor's report says one officer admitted the 3 a.m. and 5 a.m. rounds were not done and another said 'we messed up'. BOP told FBI/OIG that the SHU hallway camera had not been functioning since Thursday; the FBI seized 18 hard drives of video to confirm whether any existed. Epstein was taken off suicide watch on 7/29 and was not required to have a cellmate; his cellmate went to court on Friday and was released. The autopsy was that morning. An early internal account two days after the death, not findings; the officers and supervisor are not named here. EFTA00027972 (FBI evidence record dated 08/19/2019, case 90A-NY-3151227; companion EFTA00027962): items seized on 08/10/2019 were (1) a torn sheet, collected at 3:40 PM from SHU cell #220 on L-Tier; (2) clothing released from New York Presbyterian Hospital, collected at 4:26 PM; and (3) miscellaneous papers and an MP-3 player. The companion record logs two further items (1B20, 1B21) seized from the MCC on 08/15/2019. Evidence-log entries as printed; no analysis results are in the text read, and the agents and the MCC lieutenant are not named here. EFTA00028000 (emails dated Aug 27–28, 2019): SDNY drafts a letter to the Office of Chief Medical Examiner describing contents of the OCME file that SDNY does not want disclosed and how they came to be disclosed, after a heads-up call to OCME's general counsel. A supervisor advises 'operating on the assumption this letter, too, may someday be made public', so 'the less we say about specifics, the better'. He suggests first asking what OCME actually needs, and requesting the return of a 302 by phone only unless OCME pushes for it in writing. Internal drafting views; the final letter and the file's contents are not in the text read. EFTA00028094 (emails dated Oct 28, 2021): Epstein's brother asks BOP for video from the camera outside the SHU on August 9, 2019; a list of inmates on the tier with their placement and transfer details; the identities of those directing action on the tier and of who was in the cell with the EMTs; and any incident report. He says he is trying to find out why 'normal protocol was not followed' in moving the body before the medical examiner could photograph the scene. An AUSA, unsure how much fits a FOIA request, notes the video is in FBI and USAO custody because it was seized from BOP, and the request is passed to a BOP contact. His account and claims are his own; it follows the already-mapped earlier requests from the same correspondent.

v3.65 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 28). EFTA00028434 (emails dated Jul 25, 2019): after BOP's Regional Office says a written request, not necessarily a subpoena, is needed, SDNY asks by email for all documents and materials, including photographs, about 'the incident involving Jeffrey Epstein earlier this week'. BOP sends the staff memos and photos taken, asks whether SDNY must share them with Main Justice so it can make notifications on BOP's side, and SDNY asks to be told of further reports and when the investigation is complete. Correspondence as written; the memos and photos are not in the text read.

v3.68 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 31). EFTA00030733 (emails dated Sep 6–10, 2019): SDNY asks the FBI to scan a note that had been in Epstein's cell, described by the requester as 'the note complaining about prison conditions'. The FBI says the item had been moved to off-site evidence storage and was being recalled, and that the agent had understood Epstein wrote a letter and gave it to someone but had not found it in the file the MCC supplied. On Sep 10 the front and back of the note are sent. The note's text is not in the document read; the characterization is the requester's. Staff are not named here.

v3.69 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 32). EFTA00032162 (BOP Psychology Services clinical-contact record dated 07/27/2019; opening read only): Epstein is seen while on psychological observation. The note records the observation log as showing he ate, slept, showered, had a legal visit and talked with an inmate companion. In interview he said he still could not remember what happened in the SHU that caused the marks on his neck, that for the five days before it he had slept only about 30 minutes a night because of noise in the SHU, and that he was anxious about returning there. His mental status is recorded as neutral mood with logical, coherent speech. His statements are his own as recorded by the clinician; only the opening of this oversized record was read, and the clinician is not named here. EFTA00032092 (BOP chain-of-custody log forms, item m-19-00182): one form records as evidence the clothing in which Epstein was transported to an outside hospital, found August 10, 2019 at about 10:15 AM at New York Presbyterian Hospital and released at 10:32 AM that day to the institution's SIS office. This is an earlier BOP-custody leg of the clothing item that the atlas already shows the FBI collecting that afternoon. The rest of the scan is largely illegible. The forms as printed; staff are not named here. EFTA00031419 (emails dated Jun 3–4, 2020): a university faculty member received from someone a note and a CD that they claimed related to Epstein; the note reportedly said the disc held evidence of Epstein's 'murder'. An SDNY AUSA on the MCC guard case offers to receive it, and the sex-trafficking team agrees it should go to the guard-case team first and be passed on if relevant. The 'murder' wording is the unknown sender's, as relayed second-hand. The text read does not show the disc's contents or whether this is the same disc as the October 2020 mailing already in the atlas. EFTA00031699 (emails dated Nov 6, 2019): a national TV network correspondent tells SDNY that Epstein's brother says the office is withholding the full medical examiner files, keeps cancelling meetings with him, and has given him no evidence or explanation about why his brother's death was ruled a homicide, and asks for comment. Internally an SDNY staffer writes, 'At least some of this is false.' The brother's claims are his own as relayed by the press, and the internal reply is an unelaborated opinion. The journalist is not named here.

v3.70 extension (DS8 deepening pass, cut 33). At 10:41 a.m. the psychologist records consulting BOP's Central Office, listing risk factors for suicide — a high-profile case with media attention, sex-offence charges, pre-trial status and a court appearance that day — and instructing staff to notify psychology as soon as he returned from court and, if after hours, to place him on watch until a full suicide risk assessment. The OCR is low confidence: it yields time slots and handwritten times but no readable names or reliable entry-by-entry sequence, so this atlas draws no conclusion from the entries.

25DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility investigation of the 2008 NPAConfirmed

Verification: V

Span: Dec 2010–Nov 2020. Anchors: EFTA00019480 (Dec 10, 2010 Cassell asks SDFL U.S. Attorney Ferrer to investigate "the most suspicious criminal case I have ever encountered"; May 6, 2011 OPR declines on grounds of ongoing litigation; Feb 7, 2019 Cassell asks OPR to keep victims informed); EFTA00015719 (Feb 6, 2019 — DOJ opened an investigation into Acosta's role in the 2008 plea deal at Sen. Sasse's request after the Miami Herald's "Perversion of Justice" series; OPR to head it); EFTA00018568 (Aug 6, 2020 — OPR sends SDNY its 380+ page draft report on SDFL's 2006–2008 handling, plus ~30-page appendix); EFTA00020454 (Dec 8, 2020 — Relativity processing report on the OPR materials: 300,123-doc set, 5,462 with hits); EFTA00011475 (Nov 2020 Executive Summary, 14 pp.; duplicate EFTA00013359, 13 pp.). Endpoint: Nov 2020 OPR Executive Summary. Findings as stated in the summary: OPR did NOT find professional misconduct by Acosta or the other subjects in resolving the investigation through the NPA, and did not find evidence the decision was based on corruption or impermissible considerations such as Epstein's wealth, status, or associations; Acosta resisted defense efforts to return the matter to the state and refused to eliminate incarceration and sex-offender registration; the Oct 2007 "breakfast meeting" did not lead to the NPA, signed weeks earlier. OPR DID conclude Acosta exercised poor judgment in resolving the federal investigation through the NPA ("a flawed mechanism for satisfying the federal interest") and poor judgment in failing to ensure victims were notified about the state plea hearing. The full OPR report is not in DS8 — only the executive summary and the draft's processing trail; findings are reported as the summary states them. Links: 1 (the NPA under review), 2 (breach/inaction), P1 (CVRA).

v3.2 (WS5) extension: EFTA00038270 (DS8, Sep 2, 2020): DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility letter (950 Pennsylvania Ave.) to the FBI, re the OPR investigation.

v3.3 (WS1) extension — interview transcript + intake + jurisdiction (span unchanged, Dec 2010–Nov 2020; the Apr 2008 item below is a prologue leg, not a span move — coordinator's decision, see changelog §8): OPR interview of R. Will they stand up in court?"); on balancing ("we also thought it was very important that he serve some real punishment, and that he register… a lot of people are going to be questioning for a long, long time, but that's how we balanced it"); on the CEOS critique relayed by OPR counsel ("I'm not thrilled about the agreement… Epstein is getting a much better deal than the average defendant… I would have taken the guy to trial unless the victims were clearly against it"). The OPR intake leg. Apr 21, 2008 — AUSA's OPR self-report of conflict of interest (EFTA00208240, DS9, 3 pp., prologue leg): during pre-indictment plea negotiations the AUSA provided Epstein's counsel a series of possible attorneys for victims' civil-damages counsel, including Humberto Ocariz, "a friend of my boyfriend" (later "a friend of a close friend"); Epstein's counsel selected Ocariz; after conferring, the office decided it should not select victims' counsel and a Special Master (pro bono) would; Ocariz was NOT selected. The AUSA self-reports the allegation. The memo also narrates Operation Leap Year background: 25+ minor victims identified; PBPD → State Attorney → FBI → USAO; state grand jury indicted only 3 counts of solicitation of adults; indictment package prepared; counter-proposal (state plea + sex-offender registration + jail + damages); Acosta meeting; appeal to Washington (2 weeks); two-track drafting (NPA + federal plea agreement/information). Aug 24, 2020 — OPR planning to invite all known Epstein victims to a meeting "in order to announce the results of OPR's investigation into SDFL's non-prosecution agreement with Epstein" (EFTA00032211, DS8, 1 p.). Jan 29, 2019 — OIG letter (Horowitz) to 15 House members (EFTA00811997, DS9, 2 pp.): OIG does NOT have jurisdiction over DOJ attorneys' litigation/legal decisions; exclusive jurisdiction is OPR (IG Act §8E(b)(3)); OIG has objected to this limitation for 30 years. Explains why OPR, not OIG, investigated the NPA. Note: the OPR Executive Summary copies (EFTA00011475 / EFTA00013359 / EFTA00023059 / EFTA00095558 / EFTA00095727 / EFTA01250797 / EFTA01726257) are multiple copies of one summary; EFTA00011475 + EFTA00013359 are already Story 25 anchors. The summary's findings as read: all five subjects did NOT commit professional misconduct re the NPA's development/negotiation/approval; BUT OPR concludes Acosta's decision to resolve the investigation through the NPA "constitutes poor judgment" ("a flawed mechanism for satisfying the federal interest"); Acosta exercised poor judgment in failing to make certain the state would notify victims about the state plea hearing; victims "were not treated with the forthrightness and sensitivity expected by the Department."

Mar 24, 2011 — Daily Beast email to Roy Black: the Daily Beast received a letter from former US Attorney Alex Acosta describing the NPA negotiations; per the Daily Beast's summary, Acosta's letter says Epstein's defense team (a) negotiated in bad faith, agreeing to terms then appealing to DOJ in Washington; (b) investigated prosecutors' personal lives/families to discredit/disqualify two prosecutors — attempt failed; (c) threatened Acosta that his "excessive zeal" could become a book (EFTA00664159 — cite as the Daily Beast's summary of Acosta's letter, not as the letter itself). May 18, 2010 — Palm Beach Post: Podhurst Orseck sued Epstein claiming he refused to pay its $2 million legal bill for representing more than a dozen young women; Epstein had agreed to pay for an attorney for 33 women; the firm's claim is that failure to pay "constitutes 'a material breach'" of the NPA (the firm's allegation in its suit, labeled as such) (EFTA00190244).

Verification and review scope

Completed DS8 passes through v3.82: the actionable first-open pass, non-protected substantive deepening pass, and 1,050-document protected pass are complete at their stated depths. The protected pass added 191 anchors. The cumulative atlas now contains 2,458 story-anchor references across all sets, 82 mapped stories and 139 fragments. These are surveyed counts, not a corpus census.

The inherited 4,167-document partial queue now comprises 3,899 condensed text-layer reads, 82 opening-only reads, four structure scans, 55 near-duplicates with residual lines read, and 127 bulk items dropped after earlier screening. The image queue contains 223 lower-confidence OCR reads and 165 “No Images Produced” placeholders. The two queues overlap by 86 IDs and must not be added as distinct-document totals. The two earlier capped skips were characterized without an established story connection.

Reading method: condensed reads inspect lines not already read in another document or packet, omitting repeated lines, selected address headers and confidentiality footers. This does not establish human review or a full page-image audit. Opening-only reads and scans are not full reads. A dropped bulk item is a screening decision, not proof it contains no story.

Still open: completing the 82 opening-only reads and four structure scans; reassessing the 127 screened bulk items if warranted; image confirmation of OCR-dependent details, especially EFTA00032184 and the two P20 deeds; 66 deferred Amex/mega documents. The House Oversight full pass and DS9 torrent remain deferred. DS8 is not represented as fully read.

The source crew reports 33 primary and 25 independent checks passing for each protected-pass cut, with disclosed adaptations for the changed reading scope. Publication review reconciled the supplied ledgers and anchor lists and checked the site output; it did not repeat source-level validation against the full corpus. Victim and witness narratives are minimized in this public copy; placeholders never establish distinct-person counts or cross-document identity.

A slice whose method was capped FTS sweeps cannot distinguish "no story" from "story not yet found" in its unsampled remainder.

EXPLICIT OPEN ENDS

Open flags

  • Interlochen proffer attribution: the earlier description of Gary Bloxsome as Interlochen’s counsel is withdrawn pending source review. The proffer leg is not relied on to establish an Interlochen event.
  • MCC records: Aug 12 interview participation accounts, Aug 10 timing milestones, July 25 watch labels and tape-conversion paperwork remain qualified or unresolved. A changed plan or different event definition may explain an apparent discrepancy; no intentional misconduct is inferred.
  • Property deeds: the 2011 conveyances at EFTA00020949 and EFTA00020959 rest on lower-confidence OCR and require image confirmation.
  • Anchor eligibility: IDs previously mentioned only in queue notes or range boundaries were excluded by the crew’s strict novelty check. They are not silently added here; a mention alone does not establish a substantive citation.
  • “Lawrence H. Summers” in the 2014 will: identity with P12’s Larry Summers is not established; no document states the equation.
  • Nidal / “Ronen Cohen”: whether they are different people is not established. The Barak-traveled-as-Cohen hypothesis remains unproven.
  • DS9’s 23 inaccessible files: the torrent route is explicitly deferred. Their status remains unclassified, not deleted.
